questions: How many devices did you fabricate and measure, and how many showed resolved e/4 oscillations? The Methods name one measured device ("The device was measured", p. 9) and say "M.D.L. fabricated the devices" (p. 9).
Why were the others set aside?

Which ranges of antidot-gate voltage, field and side-gate voltage did you measure beyond the windows shown (about 100 mT in field, p. 10)? Fig. S7 shows ν = −1/3 at −2 V and 0 V only, while p. 8 says no doubling is seen "Even at the largest side-gate voltage accessible in our device", and the limit is given as "approximately 6 V" (p. 13) and as "5 V" (Fig. S6).
What does the second-best dataset at each even-denominator filling look like, for example the minimal-excitation regime at another side-gate setting or in another cooldown?

At ν = −1/2 you give ∆B = 13 ± 1.4 mT (p. 4); with ∆B1 = 40.3 ± 6.7 mT (p. 15) that is ∆B1/∆B ≈ 3.1, while the text gives p = 2, the value expected for e/4 at this filling. Which value is plotted in Fig. 4a, and how does p = 2 follow from the measured period?

The suppression temperature of the e/4 oscillations is given as "approximately 60 mK" (p. 8), "between 50 mK and 70 mK" (p. 28) and "in the same range of 30 mK to 50 mK" (p. 30). Which range is right, and which one sets your bound on the electron temperature?
Did you measure leakage from the antidot gate and the side gates at the operating voltages, and do repeated sweeps at ν = −5/2, −1/2 and 3/2 show the hysteresis you report at ν = 2/3 (Fig. S13)?

On p. 6 the text places ν = 2/3 in Fig. 3d,e and ν = −1/2 in Fig. 3g,i, while the caption assigns d–f to ν = −1/2 and g–i to ν = 2/3; on p. 7 "ν = −2/3" appears where your data are at ν = 2/3. Which labels are right?
